listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Monday, November 9. Here is what matters today. Our lead story. Nvidia has launched an investigation into reports that its chief executive, Jensen Huang, was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation. The reports come from The New York Times. The chipmaking giant says it is looking into them. Other coverage describes an alleged relationship between Huang and a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia is central to the AI boom, so this story reaches beyond one company. No findings have been reported yet. Now the front page. The San Francisco 49ers returned from their bye week with a 38 to 17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Their defense forced five turnovers. President Trump says he was only kidding when he offered UFC chief Dana White the White House press secretary job. In world news, European officials will join this week's talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. The talks are mediated by the United States. They are the first three-way round since February. The Kremlin had objected. In Washington, Congress returns this week after the midterm elections. Republicans plan to finish several outstanding issues before Democrats take control in January. Now the sections. In tech and AI, Anthropic is expanding its partnership with the General Services Administration to bring Claude to all levels of government. Vercel Labs has released a command line tool that lets AI agents drive a browser. And Simon Willison writes about handling pull request descriptions written by coding agents. In politics, NPR reports that Vice President JD Vance is looking to recast his political future after his party's midterm losses. NPR also says Trump's staffing changes show how he may approach divided government. In world news, at least 34 people died when a migrant boat sank off Senegal. Huawei is on trial in New York, accused of stealing American technology and evading sanctions. And NPR looks at how a bank collapse toppled Paraguay's president. In sports, Denver listed its whole starting lineup as questionable for tonight's game in Houston after travel delays. The 49ers lost rookie tackle Gracen Halton to a broken ankle. And in the UFC, Johnny Walker knocked out Waldo Cortes-Acosta. In Atlanta, new visuals show MARTA's Five Points redevelopment. Zoo Atlanta announced the death of Zuri, a young southern white rhino. In architecture, Chaos is bringing more AI tools into V-Ray and Enscape. Studio Gang has finished a 265-room hotel in downtown Denver. In science and nature, new analysis of a 115-million-year-old fossil points to preserved blood cells, though not everyone is convinced. NASA says this year's ozone hole was the seventh largest on record. And divers in Brazil are removing invasive sun coral near Ipanema. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's alleged relationship with Chinese spy
lead.note: Nvidia has launched an investigation into reports that its chief executive, Jensen Huang, was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation. The reports were published by The New York Times, and the chipmaking giant says it is looking into them. Other coverage describes an alleged relationship between Huang and a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia is one of the best-known companies in the AI boom, and Huang has been called the face of it, so questions about his conduct reach beyond one company. The story combines a personal matter with national security concerns about China. No findings from the company's investigation have been reported so far. For a reader who follows AI closely, it is worth watching how Nvidia handles the inquiry and what further details emerge.
